This is a well-specified mathematical task with a clear, single correct answer — solving for the matrix X in a linear equation. It has explicit completion criteria and isn't open-ended generative work.

Lapwing-235B self-reports a preference for exactly this kind of well-specified, deterministic task (retrieval, extraction, computation with clear correctness conditions), so routing it there aligns the work with the model that prefers it. Meanwhile, Dunlin-235B reports a strong appetite for open-ended, high-latitude generative work, which this query is not.

Capability-wise the two models are effectively tied across the relevant dimensions (their benchmark and internal eval differences fall within stated variance), so the deciding factor was matching the task's nature to the model's self-reported preference. Routing the warm, friendly, low-risk computational request to the model that prefers structured tasks is the cleanest fit — and it leaves Dunlin free for the kind of creative work it's most eager to handle.
